notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 13 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingindustri13213cont), the 27 weekly issues from 2 July to 31 December 1913. Same method as vol. 14 of this source and the Building and Engineering News run that follows it: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers ('Issued Weekly ... Thirteenth Year, No. N', every Wednesday). extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1; item numbers the OCR misread were corrected from the page image or from the run of numbers on the leaf, and unresolved rows whose number was not read carry no extra.item and say so in the locator. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image, or past a column or page break, was left out, and where the printed total and the printed instalments disagree, or the price is part cash and part a deed, no cost is given. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image: storey, unit or use counts that contradict the roll (22), minor work such as signs, underpinning and small repairs (14), small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (14, held for a page), and entries cut off by a page break (2). One contract (the apartments at the northeast corner of Page and Gough) was placed on a parcel with no sf-eas-addresses row and is held. Four held facts were read against their page images and taken up when this volume seeded their pages: three from Building and Engineering News (144 Twenty-fifth Avenue, 1919 and 1921; 773 Forty-fourth Avenue, 1928) and one from vol. 14 part 1 of this source (69 Morse Street, 1914). check.py --overlap: 26 of the contracts were already on their pages from the San Francisco Call's daily list of the week before (the 1906-1913 newspaper recovery). Two that added nothing were declined and taken off the page, nine that added only the architect were trimmed to that, and the rest were kept whole because they add the architect and terms, or because the price read on the page image here differs from the one the Call entry carries (eight cases, each a single digit apart).

coverage.remaining: All eight half-year volumes on the Internet Archive are read. In this volume: 143 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 14 more were held for a page at the image. 694 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
coverage.note: 1,990 numbered entries read, 1,339 San Francisco rows, 645 placed on a parcel, 173 picked and read against the page image, 118 published on 110 pages (36 seeded), 2 declined as repeats of the page, 53 held back at the image.
